claims.statement: Run explorEDA from a CLI in a repo folder, project-based like Jupyter notebooks.
Launch with npx exploreda.
Runs in different folders; maybe a global config.
For general users the CLI runs a local server.
Project/workspace files live on disk.
Does the CLI support databases?
This is the first runtime mode to build.
File sources only in the first release; database connections are the next CLI milestone.
The CLI ships as a bin in the exploreda package (npx exploreda).
A project folder holds shared project info plus one file per analysis, like notebooks; config can live in a hidden folder or in workspace files.
No sign-in in CLI mode; one local user.
Config and storage location is the user's choice per project: everything hidden in .exploreda/ or in visible project/workspace files.
CLI v1 includes global config, file watching, and static HTML export; notebook view is not in v1.
Data files are read in place; analyses use project-relative paths by default and may reference outside paths.
CLI must be polished enough for a public launch.
Analyses are DSL v2 dashboard text (.eda), lossless for charts, fields, filters, calcs, and multiple views.
Build on the DSL v2 stack (#334→#360) after it merges; add only what files need, no syntax redesign.
Debounced autosave; outside edits win and reload the app with a notice; undo history is in memory only.

Browser loads data as the demo does; target up to ~100 MB CSV.

shape.appetite: Launch-quality local-file CLI incl. three-OS smoke, docs, example project, and demo folder-open; starts after DSL v2 merges.
shape.problem: No way to run explorEDA against a folder of files and keep analyses as committable text.
shape.recommended_shape: exploreda bin starts a localhost server serving apps/app over a project folder: project text (sources, relationships, queries) + one DSL v2 .eda per analysis; autosave, file watching, in-memory undo; demo reads the same folder via File System Access.
success_moves: Prove the project grammar (sources, relationships, all six query steps) as an exact round trip with AnalysisProject before building the folder format.
Keep exploreda-project JSON as the fallback store if the grammar proof fails, so launch is not blocked.
Put folder read/write behind one project-store port used by both the Node server and the demo's File System Access adapter.
Develop against an in-memory filesystem fake for the store and watcher; the real fs and three-OS smoke come later.
Ship the server as a separate bin build so component consumers never load Node code.
Use the existing set escape hatch so no state is lost while text gaps remain.

first_proof.question: Can sources, relationships, and all query step types be written as DSL text that round-trips AnalysisProject exactly and that an agent can write from the reference?
first_proof.artifact: Project grammar + round-trip test over every multi-source demo example + a cold-agent draft of the shop project checked with exploreda-dsl check.
first_proof.decision_rule: All examples round-trip and set covers under 5% of query lines → build the folder format on text; otherwise launch with a project JSON file and move the text form below the cut line.
first_proof.result: Passed 2026-10-12: all 6 demo projects round-trip deep-equal with 0 set lines and identical evaluated rows; cold-agent shop draft compiled with 0 diagnostics and matched demo rows. See raw/proof/results.md.
